answer_1.quote: We apply our method to two challenging tasks where LLMs are commonly utilized but their performance still lags behind humans: • Evaluation of LLM Outputs … • Constrained Text Generation …
answer_1.outputs: evaluations of LLM responses, generated stories

answer_2.quote: We evaluate BSM (and baselines) using the following four metrics. • LLM-Human Agreement (Ag). • Position Bias (PB). • Length Bias (LB). • Self‑enhancement Bias (SB). For constrained story generation we also report All Present (AP) and Missing Concepts (MC).

answer_3.quote: We use LLMs as judges after generation, e.g., pairwise evaluation with GPT‑4 for story quality and scoring per criterion for LLM output evaluation.

answer_4.quote: The MT‑Bench dataset consists of 2400 LLM responses and 3000 expert human judgements, which we use to compute LLM‑human agreement and assess criteria such as relevance, clarity, and correctness.
answer_4.guideline: Human annotators judge LLM responses on multiple criteria (e.g., relevance, clarity, accuracy, code correctness, creativity).
